papers.title: SilencioMA: A single compound that targets both MAPT and APP as a potential disease modifying therapeutic for Alzheimer's Disease
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is the most common age-related neurodegenerative disease and the leading cause of dementia worldwide. AD pathogenesis involves aggregation of amyloid-beta (A{beta}), produced from amyloidogenic proteolytic processing of Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP), and accumulation of misfolded, pathological tau (Microtubule Associated Protein Tau, MAPT). Current efforts focus on developing disease modifying therapeutics (DMTs) against single targets: A{beta} or tau. However, DMTs that concurrently target both tau and A{beta} are likely to have the greatest impact since they target both culprits of AD pathogenesis. Here we describe the development of SilencioMA, a single compound that targets both MAPT and APP messenger RNAs (mRNAs) based on silencing connected interfering oligonucleotides against MAPT and APP. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) administration of SilencioMA reduces A{beta} and tau and pathology after a single intracerebroventricular injection in 5XFAD/PS19 mice, an animal model of severe amyloidosis and tauopathy. SilencioMA does not rely on lipid nanoparticles or lipophilic conjugates for CSF administration. At the same time its modular design permits conjugation of ligands that facilitate transcytosis through the blood brain barrier, allowing systemic administration. Our findings provide proof-of-concept for a strategy that targets the dual A{beta} and tau pathologies of AD, and establishes a compelling foundation for further development of SilencioMA as a next-generation DMT for AD.

papers.title: TREM2-stimulated, PDGF-dependent macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk induces beneficial plaque remodeling in clonal hematopoiesis
papers.abstract: Background: In Jak2V617F clonal hematopoiesis, inflammatory signaling suppresses macrophage TREM2 and promotes features of plaque instability, while therapeutic TREM2 agonism reverses plaque instability by increasing fibroblasts and fibrous cap formation. We tested whether macrophage-derived PDGFB and stromal cell PDGFR? signaling mediate this response. Methods: Low allele burden (LAB) Jak2V617F atherosclerosis models were combined with inducible Pdgfb deletion in CX3CR1-lineage monocytes/macrophages or Pdgfra deletion in Col1a2-lineage fibroblast-enriched stromal cells. Mice were treated with the TREM2 agonist 4D9. Plaque composition, macrophage-fibroblast interactions, and aortic stromal cell populations were analyzed. Human WT and JAK2V617F iPSC-derived macrophages were used for validation. Results: TREM2 activation with 4D9 increased macrophage PDGFB production and promoted fibrous cap formation in LAB Jak2V617F atherosclerosis. Deletion of Pdgfb in CX3CR1-lineage cells markedly attenuated the 4D9-mediated increase in fibrous cap area and lesional PDGFR?+ cells, establishing macrophage-derived PDGFB as a key signal for the stromal response. Consistently, Col1a2-lineage Pdgfra deletion abolished the 4D9-induced fibrous cap response without significantly altering lesion or necrotic core area. Single cell RNA-seq identified increased Fmod+ and CD26/Dpp4+ fibroblast populations associated with 4D9 treatment. Fmod+ fibroblasts represented an abundant matrix-associated population, whereas CD26+ fibroblasts showed greatest enrichment, prominent extracellular matrix, collagen organization, and matrix-remodeling programs that were enhanced by 4D9 and attenuated by Pdgfra deletion. The stromal response was also associated with reduced macrophage migration-related programs and predicted chemokine communication from CD26+ fibroblasts to macrophages which was verified by macrophage migration studies. Moreover, stromal Pdgfra deletion increased lesional CCR2+ and CCR5+ macrophages. Conclusions: In a CH model of inflammatory atherosclerosis, TREM2 activation promotes a macrophage PDGFB-stromal PDGFR? pathway that expands Fmod+ and CD26+ fibroblast populations and increases fibrous cap matrix formation. CD26+ fibroblasts impair macrophage chemotaxis in a DPP4-dependent manner, suggesting reciprocal macrophage-fibroblast communication that coordinates matrix remodeling and inflammatory cell trafficking in the plaque.

papers.title: SilencioM: silencing connected interfering oligonucleotides against MAPT as a potential disease modifying therapeutic for tauopathies
papers.abstract: Tauopathies are a diverse group of neurodegenerative diseases whose pathogenesis involves brain accumulation of misfolded, pathological tau (Microtubule Associated Protein Tau, MAPT). More than twenty tauopathies have been identified thus far that collectively impact millions of people worldwide, of which the most common is Alzheimer's disease (AD). Despite substantial efforts to develop drugs for tauopathies, no effective treatments currently exist, highlighting the urgent need for therapeutics to combat these prevalent and ruinous neurodegenerative diseases. Strategies that target tau are likely to have the greatest impact since tau is the proximal cause of their pathogenesis. Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) have emerged as a powerful class of precision therapeutics that silence disease-causing genes through RNA interference with favorable safety profiles. Delivery challenges are rapidly being addressed, and siRNA-based approaches are poised to transform the therapeutic landscape of neurological diseases. In this study, we describe SilencioM (Silencing connected interfering oligonucleotides against MAPT) and show its efficacy in markedly reducing tau pathology after a single intracerebroventricular injection in PS19 mice, a mouse model of severe tauopathy. SilencioM targets human, primate, rat and mouse ortholog genes; thus, the same compound can proceed from efficacy studies to Investigational New Drug Application (IND)-enabling studies. SilencioM is simple to manufacture and is administered without encapsulation in lipid nanoparticles and without requirements for lipophilic conjugation, making it a promising candidate for further development as a novel therapeutic for tauopathies, including AD.

papers.title: CD8+ T-cells protect against experimental atherosclerosis through antigen specific interactions in the plaque
authors: B. A. J. A. van de Sluis
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease with a significant adaptive immune component. CD8+ T cells accumulate in plaques and display signatures of antigen-specific activation. However, whether this accumulation is driven by local antigen recognition and what functional consequences follow, remains poorly understood. Here we address this gap of knowledge using loss- and gain-of-function experiments. Atherosclerotic Rag-/-Ldlr-/- mice received adoptively transferred wildtype or antigen-restricted CD8+ T cells alongside CD4+ T cells to distinguish antigen-specific from antigen-independent responses. In a complementary model, ApobOVA-TGxLdlr-/- mice, expressing an ovalbumin-tagged variant of the atherosclerosis-associated ApoB100 protein, enabled OT-I CD8+ T cells to function as atherosclerosis-antigen-specific CD8+ T cells. T-cell distribution, activation and phenotype were assessed systemically and within lesions, plaque burden and composition were quantified histologically. Wildtype CD8+ T cells accumulated significantly more in aortic lesions compared to antigen-restricted CD8+ T cells, and exhibited increased activation, exhaustion and cytokine secretion, indicating that plaque-infiltrating T cells are predominantly antigen-specific. Perturbing antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell interactions significantly decreased plaque stability index, suggesting a protective role for antigen-specific CD8+ T cells. In ApobOVA-TGxLdlr-/- mice, OT-I T cells accumulated at high frequency in the liver, consistent with hepatic ApoB100-expression, and were found in circulation and aorta. Histological analysis revealed reduced plaque burden in OT-I recipients, reproducing an atheroprotective effect of antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell responses. Plaque reduction coincided with reduced TUNEL, but similar Caspase 3 staining, suggesting OT-I transfer results in reduced secondary necrosis. In line with this, CD47 expression in OT-I recipient mice was reduced and in vitro, OT-I but not antigen non-specific CD8+ T cells reduced expression of CD47 on OVA-presenting foam cells. CD8+ T-cell accumulation in experimental atherosclerosis is driven primarily by antigen-specific interactions and such responses are associated with plaque stabilization and reduced lesion formation, potentially through induction of apoptosis and prevention of secondary necrosis

papers.title: Relative expression of THY1 and PDGFRA in equine endometrosis in relation to severity, histopathological features and endometrial transcripts
papers.abstract: Equine endometrosis is a degenerative uterine disease characterized by periglandular fibrosis and represents a major cause of subfertility in mares. While stromal cell activation results in pathological tissue remodeling, the involvement of cell-surface integrators (THY1) and growth factor receptors (PDGFRA) was not researched. This study evaluated the relative mRNA expression of THY1 and PDGFRA across Kenney and Doig (KD) endometrosis categories and specific histopathological features. Additionally, transcriptomic correlation profiles between target genes and markers of myofibroblast differentiation (ACTA2), cellular proliferation (MKI67), and steroid hormone receptors (ESR1, PGR) were analyzed. Endometrial samples (n = 47) were quantified using RT-qPCR. Relative mRNA expression of THY1 differed significantly across KD categories (p = 0.014), exhibiting a transient upregulation in category IIA compared with category I (p = 0.009) and category IIB (p = 0.002). Furthermore, THY1 relative mRNA expression was significantly elevated in tissues with glandular basal lamina disruption (p = 0.022). Conversely, PDGFRA relative mRNA expression remained stable across disease categories (p > 0.05). THY1 relative mRNA expression correlated very strongly with ACTA2 ({rho} = 0.875, p < 0.001) and strongly with ESR1 ({rho} = 0.652, p < 0.001). PDGFRA relative mRNA expression exhibited a very strong positive correlation with ESR1 ({rho} = 0.864, p < 0.001) and a strong positive correlation with MKI67 ({rho} = 0.674, p < 0.001). These results indicate that THY1 transcription is transiently induced during early stromal remodeling and basal lamina loss, whereas PDGFRA maintains constitutive transcript stability. Observed co-expression profiles reflect statistical co-variation among stromal remodeling, proliferative, and steroid-responsive cell populations in bulk tissue.

papers.title: sPLA2 inhibitor-loaded nanoparticles mitigate spontaneous osteoarthritis in guinea pigs
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease lacking effective disease-modifying therapies. Secreted phospholipase A2 (sPLA2), a key upstream regulator of inflammatory lipid mediators, has been implicated in OA pathogenesis, but its therapeutic potential in age-related OA remains unclear. Here, we evaluated the role of sPLA2 and the efficacy of nanoparticle-mediated sPLA2 inhibition in a spontaneous OA model using female Dunkin-Hartley (DH) guinea pigs. We first characterized OA progression and observed age-dependent increases in cartilage degeneration, synovitis, oxidative stress, and sPLA2 expression and enzymatic activity. We then developed sPLA2 inhibitor (thioetheramide-PC)-loaded nanoparticles (sPLA2i-NPs) and demonstrated their superior ability, compared to free inhibitor, to prevent IL-1{beta}-induced cartilage degeneration in guinea pig cartilage explants. In vivo, intra-articular administration of sPLA2i-NPs from 3 months of age significantly attenuated cartilage destruction, synovial inflammation, and osteophyte formation in 7- and 10-month-old guinea pigs. These structural improvements were accompanied by normalization of anabolic and catabolic gene expression and a marked reduction in synovial fluid sPLA2 activity. Importantly, longitudinal gait analysis revealed that sPLA2i-NP treatment preserved limb loading, propulsion, and locomotor performance, demonstrating functional recovery. No systemic toxicity was observed following long-term treatment. Collectively, our findings identify sPLA2 as a key driver of spontaneous OA and establish nanoparticle-mediated sPLA2 inhibition as a promising disease-modifying strategy for age-related OA.

papers.title: Elevated precontractile calcium set point is sustained by limited PMCA1 export in dystrophic muscle
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is caused by loss of dystrophin and marked by elevated muscle calcium, usually attributed to contraction-induced membrane damage. Whether calcium rises before muscle can contract, and what sustains it, is unresolved. In Caenorhabditis elegans embryos and patient-derived human myoblasts, dystrophic muscle carries an elevated resting calcium set point before contraction is possible. Embryonic calcium is elevated 400 minutes after fertilization, before movement is detectable or the neuromuscular junction forms. Silencing the plasma membrane calcium pump gene mca-1 raises calcium in wild-type but not dystrophic animals, whereas silencing its paralogue raises it in both: the limitation is specific to that export route. Dystrophic human myoblasts have less pump; pump inhibition or silencing increases calcium preferentially in healthy cells, and raising pump expression lowers calcium most in dystrophic cells. Constrained calcium export is an early, continuing determinant of the dystrophic set point.

papers.title: Systematic comparison of gliflozins identifies a selective anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition
papers.abstract: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide important cardiorenal benefits in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their effects on vascular calcification remain conflicting. Whether potential anti-calcifying effects are shared across gliflozins or involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition is unknown. Methods: We systematically compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a high-phosphate diet-induced mouse model of vascular calcification and complementary ex vivo and in vitro models, including rodent and human vascular tissues and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Aortic transcriptional response was investigated by RNA sequencing. VSMC calcification, proliferation, migration, viability, glucose uptake and bioenergetics were investigated using complementary cellular assays, including OsteoSense staining, Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, radiolabeled 2-deoxyglucose uptake and Seahorse ATP rate analysis. SGLT2/1 expression was examined by RT-qPCR, Western blotting and immunofluorescence. We also evaluated sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, and mizagliflozin, a selective SGLT1 inhibitor. Results: Among the three gliflozins, only canagliflozin significantly reduced aortic calcification in vivo. Its anti-calcifying effect was also observed in rodent aortic rings, human vascular explants, cultured VSMCs and aortic rings from diabetic db/db mice. Aortic RNA-seq revealed that canagliflozin partially reversed HPD-induced transcriptional alterations, including changes in pro-calcific signaling and cellular metabolism, while some endothelial and inflammatory responses were shared among gliflozins. In mouse VSMCs, canagliflozin reduced calcification across all tested concentrations, dose-dependently decreased osteogenic marker expression, and reduced proliferation and migration. Increased apoptotic and damaged cell fractions were observed at higher concentrations, but not at lower concentrations. Canagliflozin also reduced glucose uptake and mitochondrial ATP production, without significantly affecting glycolytic ATP production. Neither dapagliflozin nor empagliflozin reproduced these cellular and metabolic effects at any of the concentrations tested. SGLT2 and SGLT1 expression was low or undetectable in vascular tissues and cells, and neither sotagliflozin nor mizagliflozin reproduced the anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin in vivo or in vitro. Conclusions: Canagliflozin exhibits a selective anti-calcifying profile among the gliflozins tested, associated with changes in VSMC responses and cellular metabolism. These findings suggest that its vascular protective effects may involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition.

papers.title: Midlife nonlinearities across scale in Biondi body amyloid formation in the human choroid plexus
papers.abstract: Human choroid plexus epithelial cells (CPECs), which produce cerebrospinal fluid and form the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier, accumulate discrete intracellular amyloid inclusions called Biondi bodies (BBs). Using systematic manual and machine learning approaches on the choroid plexus glomus, we determined the percentages of CPECs containing thioflavin S-stained BBs as well as BB load and spatial distributions in whole slide images from 77 cases across the human lifespan. On average, BB prevalence was near zero until age 40, rose steeply in the 5th and 6th decades, and exceeded 50% after age 70. As prevalence plateaued, BB load continued to rise with age. Accelerated BB accumulation was seen in two cases of diabetic ketoacidosis, including a 16-year-old, while an 85-year-old with the relatively rare APOE2/E2 genotype had fewer BBs than expected. BB prevalence in the choroid plexus glomus was not associated with Alzheimer's disease, but was lower in females than males. Notably, spatial clustering of BBs was universal across cases while nearest-neighbor analyses suggested cell-to-cell, prion-like BB spread that can account for the nonlinearities seen at tissue and population scales. The abrupt, nonlinear BB accumulation during midlife coincides with or precedes other common aging-associated neuropathologies of the human brain, consistent with broad BB and choroid plexus contributions to brain aging and disease.

papers.title: Hypoxemia is an Independent Risk Factor for Perioperative Thrombosis at High Altitude: A Retrospective Study of 11,084 Patients
papers.abstract: Objective Perioperative thrombosis occurs at a significantly higher rate at high altitudes compared to low altitudes, severely threatening the safety of surgical patients. This study aims to determine the independent risk factors for perioperative thrombosis in high-altitude environments, providing a scientific basis for early clinical screening and targeted intervention. Methods Clinical data from 11,084 surgical patients were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were categorized into thrombosis and non-thrombosis groups based on the occurrence of postoperative thrombosis. Baseline characteristics, operative variables, and laboratory indicators were collected, encompassing 21 potential risk factors including arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2). Univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression (forward stepwise likelihood ratio method) were performed using SPSS 27.0 to identify independent risk factors for perioperative thrombosis. The predictive performance of the model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), calibration plots, and nomograms. Results Of the 11,084 patients, 1,631 (14.7%) developed thrombosis. Univariate analysis showed that varicose veins, hemoglobin levels, Preoperative hospital stay, body mass index (BMI), D-dimer, partial pressure of oxygen, and interleukin-6 were significantly associated with thrombosis (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified varicose veins,Preoperative hospital stay, elevated BMI, erythrocytosis, elevated D-dimer, hypoxemia, and elevated interleukin-6 as independent risk factors for thrombosis (P < 0.05). The predictive model demonstrated strong discrimination, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.862 (95% CI: 0.848-0.876), a sensitivity of 0.790, and a specificity of 0.773. Among the individual risk factors, hypoxemia exhibited the highest diagnostic performance, yielding an AUC of 0.732 and a sensitivity of 0.763. Conclusion The incidence of perioperative thrombosis at high altitudes is elevated, with hypoxemia serving as an independent predictor beyond traditional risk factors. Clinical management should prioritize correcting pre- and postoperative hypoxic states. Furthermore, implementing individualized prophylaxis that accounts for other risk factors such as multiple surgeries, advanced age, anemia, and coagulation-fibrinolysis system abnormalities is crucial to mitigating thrombotic risk.

papers.title: Failed allogeneic corneal lenticules show fibrosis and identity loss without dominant T cell rejection
papers.abstract: Failed allogeneic corneal stromal lenticules develop progressive opacity, but the state of the implanted tissue is unknown. Here we show that six explants from three patients occupy a fibrotic integration-failure state with scar-matrix production and loss of corneal identity without a dominant T cell rejection program. Scar-matrix, transparency and corneal-identity programs separated every patient from eight unimplanted donor controls, the last defined by independent human single-cell references. Calibrated immune programs and repertoire reconstruction distinguished the explants from canonical adaptive rejection. Exchange reduced interface reflectivity initially, followed by recurrent opacity in two patients and corneal steepening with declining uncorrected acuity in the third. In non-scarring rabbit repair, identity moved toward the uninjured state as backscatter returned toward normal despite increasing similarity to the explant-derived expression signature. Within one culture experiment, marked scar suppression accompanied opposite identity responses. Tacrolimus and rapamycin likewise suppressed canonical rejection while moving identity in opposite directions. Resveratrol combined reduced scar-associated programs and increased identity with improved graft appearance in the source study. These findings establish classic-rejection activity and tissue integration as separable axes and direct treatment of failed lenticules from escalating immunosuppression toward control of stromal remodeling and preservation of corneal identity.

papers.title: Transmural Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Nominates Candidate Disease Programs in Human Necrotizing Enterocolitis
papers.abstract: Background & Aims: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening disease of premature infants marked by inflammation, ischemia, mucosal injury, and, in advanced cases, necrosis extending into deeper layers of the intestinal wall. Because NEC affects specialized, interacting cells in a developing intestine, we used single-nucleus transcriptomics to build a transmural, cell-type-resolved map and nominate hypothesis-generating disease programs distinct from maturation. Methods: Full-thickness intestinal specimens from fetal/prenatal controls, acute NEC cases, and infant controls were analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq). Fetal and infant samples served as developmental references. Analyses included cell annotation, NEC-versus-infant differential expression, gene ontology (GO), cross-lineage recurrence, cell death signatures, and developmental maturity. Results: We profiled 53,735 nuclei by snRNA-seq and resolved 34 epithelial, stromal, vascular, immune, neuronal, glial, and smooth muscle populations. We used a morphology-based nuclei scoring system for sample selection that predicted high-quality transcript recovery. NEC nuclei were represented across this cellular landscape, with recurrent gene-expression changes suggesting shared inflammatory recruitment, antimicrobial/redox defense, stress adaptation, complement/vascular activation, reduced homeostatic signaling, and cell death-associated regulation. Developmental maturity analysis identified fetal-like expression levels in subsets of NEC-regulated genes. Proliferative crypt populations retained DNA repair/cell-cycle programs with inflammatory, hypoxic, and ER-stress features, while absorptive enterocytes showed reduced digestive, transport, detoxification, and terminal villus-function programs. Secretory-lineage changes implicated goblet mucus-barrier responses with reduced glycosylation, trafficking, and hydration; enteroendocrine changes in epithelial defense, metabolic stress, and neural signaling; and Paneth cell retention of antimicrobial effector transcripts despite altered ER quality control, autophagy, and granule delivery in NEC. Non-epithelial programs implicated stromal Wnt/BMP niche loss, impaired lymphatic drainage/scavenging, macrophage cytokine activation with reduced clearance machinery, neuroglial circuit defects, and altered smooth muscle contraction-relaxation balance. Conclusions: This single nuclear intestinal cell atlas nominates multicellular programs that may govern NEC initiation, progression toward tissue destruction, and resolution toward functional recovery.

papers.title: Explainable Multimodal Prognostic Modeling Uncovers New Clinically Relevant Pathological Features in a Multi-Institutional Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Cohort
papers.abstract: Although many patients with a well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PanNET) are cured after surgical resection, it is hard to predict outcome in these patients. Current prognostic assessment relies largely on Ki-67 proliferation index, tumor stage, and established adverse pathologic features, such as vascular and perineural invasion. However, individually, these variables incompletely explain why patients with similar clinicopathologic profiles sometimes experience markedly different outcomes. To address this challenge, we assembled three independent cohorts with a surgically resected PanNET. In total, we included 1,438 patients with approximately 30,000 histology images, and approximately 12,000 person-years of follow-up. We separately modeled structured clinicopathologic information with Cox regression and tumor-centered pathology images with deep learning on an internal cohort treated at Johns Hopkins Hospital and performed multimodal continuous-time survival modeling to reveal which clinical and pathologic features are most important in predicting patient outcome. Across Cox models of censored time to recurrence-free survival, a text-based clinicopathological model that incorporated known prognosticators achieved a C-index of approximately 0.87, the image-based histology model approximately 0.80, and decision-level late multimodal fusion approximately 0.88 on the internal test set. The clinical model demonstrated strong prognostic discrimination using established risk factors, mainly relying on the TNM stage and Ki-67 index. Primary tumor histology retained substantial prognostic signal, with analysis restricted to tumor-centered regions to reduce reliance on unrelated tissues that might indirectly indicate disease extent. Interpretation of high-attention image tiles revealed regions of importance in the primary tumor, including recognized adverse morphologic features such as the leading edge of the tumor and foci of vascular or perineural invasion. Unexpectedly, intratumoral and peritumoral stroma accounted for nearly 50% of the model's high-attention regions, suggesting that the stroma may yield equal prognostic information to neoplastic cells in recurrence-prediction models. To test generalizability, we further evaluated the trained models in independent cohorts from two institutions with different demographics, where discrimination varied by site (mean late-fusion C-indices of 0.864 and 0.723). Together with the improved discrimination achieved through late fusion, our findings suggest that current clinicopathologic variables can be modeled to form reliable prognosticators, and that routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained slides of the primary tumor contain additional prognostically important information not fully captured by conventional clinicopathologic assessment, such that together, the two sources provide complementary information.

papers.title: Histopathological and virus-associated features of Boid Inclusion Body Disease in Boa constrictor
papers.abstract: Boid inclusion body disease (BIBD) is a reptarenavirus-induced fatal disease of boid snakes that, while diagnosed with ease due to the pathognomonic intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies (IB), is not yet fully characterized pathomorphologically and with regards to its pathogenesis. The present study retrospectively investigated a random cohort of 50 captive male and female boa constrictors of variable age (neonate to 25 years) for histopathological changes and in situ viral protein (nucleoprotein, NP, and glycoprotein 2, GP2) expression patterns. IB formation and NP expression were scored semiquantitatively. The vast majority of snakes (42/50; 84%) exhibited histopathological changes; these mainly (39/42; 93%) represented inflammatory processes that most frequently affected the gastrointestinal tract. Overall, IB and NP scores were significantly higher in the more recent cases (2020-2025) compared to the older cases (2000-2003). NP scores did not differ between age groups or sex, but were lower in animals with clinical signs and higher in those with histopathological changes. No statistically significant association was found between NP scores and inflammatory processes, neither in general nor in individual organs. GP2 expression, as an indicator of virion assembly, was less consistent than NP expression and generally restricted to individual cells with and without IBs. There was no histological evidence of overt damage in infected cells. Jointly, the results indicate different phases of restrictive and systemic viral replication that are not directly associated with pathological processes and/or clinical signs.

papers.title: Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy of optically cleared human head-and-neck organs: three-dimensional tissue assessment and histological correlation
authors: M. F. C. M. van den Hout
papers.abstract: Conventional histology provides detailed cellular information but only a partial view of the three-dimensional (3D) organisation of head-and-neck tissues. We investigated whether optical tissue clearing combined with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) could visualise the microanatomy of large head-and-neck specimens and relate volumetric features to conventional histology. Non-neoplastic human palatine tonsil, cervical lymph node, tongue and parotid gland specimens were cleared with a solvent-based protocol, labelled with small-molecule dyes and imaged by LSFM, with haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology as a morphological reference. LSFM visualised the characteristic architecture of each tissue, including lymphoid follicles and crypt epithelium in tonsil, cortex, paracortex and follicles in lymph node, epithelium and intrinsic muscle fibres in tongue, and lobules, ducts and adipocytes in parotid. Following structures through successive optical sections revealed their continuity and branching over long distances, information not available from single sections. Tongue epithelial measurements were comparable with H&E, and segmentation enabled volumetric quantification of structures such as the tongue epithelium and parotid adipocytes. Optical clearing and LSFM thus provide a feasible single workflow for volumetric investigation of human head-and-neck microanatomy. These data establish a 3D morphological reference with potential applications in cancer research and staging, computational image analysis and anatomical education, to be further developed through larger donor cohorts and specific labelling.

papers.title: Comparison of Hydroponic and Substrate-Based Methods for Screening Pea Genotypes for Resistance to Fusarium oxysporum.
papers.abstract: Abstract Pea (Pisum sativum L.) is one of the most economically and nutritionally important legumes due to its protein, vitamin, and mineral content. It also represents a source of income for producers. One of the major constraints on pea production is vascular wilt caused by the fungus Fusarium oxysporum. One strategy for disease management is the use of resistant varieties, which highlights the need for efficient methodologies to evaluate genotype responses to the pathogen. The objective of this study was to compare the efficiency of hydroponic and conventional substrate-based methods for evaluating the responses of pea genotypes to F. oxysporum under semi-controlled conditions. The hydroponic method used a modified Hoagland and Arnon nutrient solution with adjusted nutrient concentrations, whereas the conventional substrate-based method used plastic bags containing one kilogram of peat. The pathogen inoculum was obtained from pea plants affected by the disease in the municipality of Puerres, Narino, Colombia (isolate FPUE02). In both methods, six pea genotypes and an uninoculated control were evaluated using a randomized complete block design with three replicates. Plant growth parameters, disease incidence, and disease severity were recorded. The hydroponic method showed greater sensitivity in discriminating among susceptible genotypes and facilitated the monitoring of disease progression in the roots. These results highlight the potential of the hydroponic method as a tool for the phytopathological evaluation of pea germplasm.

papers.title: Role of the gut microbiota in the remodelling of the jejunal, colonic, hepatic and blood proteomes in a mouse model of Anorexia Nervosa
papers.abstract: Background: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a typical form of eating disorder characterized by a severe body weight loss, a fear of gaining weight and dysmorphophobia. This disorder is associated with both psychiatric comorbidities and multi-organ dysfunctions. Increasing evidence suggests a role of the gut microbiota in the onset or maintenance of AN. Although a dysbiosis has been reported in patients with AN, the physiological consequences of this dysbiosis remain poorly documented. To gain further insight into the role of the gut microbiota in the pathophysiology of AN, we used the murine Activity-based Anorexia (ABA) model and compared the remodelling of the jejunal, colonic, hepatic and blood proteomes occurring in male mice with intact gut microbiota, as well as in gut microbiota-depleted animals. Results: We observed a significant proteome remodelling in several organs in response to the ABA model. More than 250 proteins involved in energy metabolism, catabolic processes, lipid metabolism, ghrelin regulation, and immune functions were found to show altered abundance in ABA mice compared to control mice. We observed in addition in the blood of ABA mice a significant increase in the level of circulating proteasome. By comparing mice treated or not with antibiotics, we identified 75 proteins whose regulation in ABA mice is gut-microbiota dependent. The other identified proteins were similarly affected in ABA mice with intact or depleted gut microbiota, suggesting that these factors are mainly regulated by food starvation and physical activity, and not directly by the gut microbiota. We finally confirmed that ORM2, a protein identified as significantly decreased in the plasma of ABA mice, is also decreased in the blood of patients suffering from AN. Conclusion: Our results demonstrate that the Activity-Based Anorexia model is associated with an extensive proteome remodelling in several organs and tissues. We highlight in addition that some of these targets are regulated in a gut microbiota-dependent manner, thereby reinforcing the hypothesis of a role of the gut microbiota in Anorexia Nervosa. Together, our study provides a valuable resource to better delineate the impact of undernutrition and maladaptive physical activity on the proteome of various organs and the role of the gut bacteria in the pathophysiology of Anorexia Nervosa.

papers.title: Pathology foundation-model embeddings reveal a morphological landscape of breast lesions beyond diagnostic categories
papers.abstract: Background: Despite rapid advances in computational pathology, including foundation-model embeddings, most approaches remain classifier-based. Breast lesion pathology is an area of unmet clinicopathological need and a compelling setting for morphology-based modeling: diagnostic categories occupy overlapping morphological spectra and reflect heterogeneous pathways of tumor development, thereby posing substantial challenges for pathological diagnosis and subsequent clinical decision-making. However, approaches to delineate morphological continua across diagnostic categories and tumor development remain understudied. Here, we leveraged morphology-based foundation-model embeddings to define a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories and dissect how these embeddings could reflect a pathobiological continuum or sequence associated with tumor development. Methods: To model breast lesion categories in continuous morphology space, we established a leakage-controlled, patient-aware workflow using the frozen foundation model Prov-GigaPath and the BReAst Carcinoma Subtyping (BRACS) dataset, a pathologist-annotated hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) breast lesion dataset spanning normal tissue, benign proliferative lesions, atypical lesions, ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and invasive carcinoma (IC). Using the BRACS training split, we defined a train-derived principal component analysis (PCA) morphology space. We then performed two complementary analyses: normal-rooted k-nearest-neighbor (kNN)-Dijkstra graph-distance scoring to derive a trajectory-like morphology score without imposing the full ordinal diagnostic sequence; pairwise Energy distance and squared maximum mean discrepancy with a radial-basis-function kernel (RBF-MMD2) to quantify order-free distributional separation among diagnostic categories. Validation and test data were projected into the train-defined reference space to assess reproducibility. Results: Prov-GigaPath embeddings defined a train-derived morphology space with category-associated organization. Without imposing the full diagnostic sequence, normal-rooted kNN-Dijkstra graph distances recovered a trajectory-like morphology arrangement from normal/benign to malignant lesions. Order-free Energy distance and RBF-MMD2 further supported graded separation among lesion categories. Validation and test datasets preserved the pathological organization. Furthermore, morphological embeddings dissected DCIS heterogeneity associated with concurrent invasive carcinoma, without requiring additional molecular information. Conclusions: Leveraging morphology-based foundation-model embeddings, we defined a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories, allowing nuanced positioning of breast lesions along a pathobiological continuum associated with tumor development. Our approaches pave the way for extracting biologically and clinically relevant information from routine histopathology to guide molecular testing, individualized risk assessment, and cost-efficient clinicopathological decision-making.

papers.title: Short-term changes in a chicken comb vascular model mimicking port-wine stain after synchronous ultrasound parallel beam treatment: an exploratory study
papers.abstract: Synchronous ultrasound parallel beam (SUPERB) technology heats the mid-dermis without relying on hemoglobin as an optical chromophore, but its effect on the cutaneous microvasculature has not been reported. We examined short-term responses of a hypervascular chicken comb model to SUPERB treatment combined with applicator compression. In six adult roosters, two sites on the left comb surface each received a single pulse of 3 to 5 J after compression blanching, and the right surface served as a within-animal control. Full-thickness biopsies were taken immediately after treatment and on days 3 and 7; one rooster died on day 2, leaving five for analysis. Hematoxylin and eosin sections were assessed descriptively by a blinded pathologist, and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) positive area and Masson collagen area were quantified on day 7 at the animal level. Reduced microvascular caliber and fewer intraluminal erythrocytes were recorded at 1 of 10 sites immediately after treatment, 8 of 10 sites on day 3 and 8 of 9 evaluable sites on day 7. On day 7, VEGF-A positive area was lower on the treated side in all five animals (11.5% vs. 20.5%; mean paired difference -9.1 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -13.3 to -4.9; exact Wilcoxon p = 0.0625, the smallest value attainable with five pairs). Collagen area did not change consistently. Tissue temperature and perfusion were not measured, and no sham-compression group was included. These hypothesis-generating findings support controlled studies that separate the effects of compression and ultrasound energy.

papers.title: Pharmacological activation of mitophagy prevents calcific aortic valve disease by targeting dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication
papers.abstract: Abstract Background and Aims: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) lacks pharmacologic therapy. Mitophagy impairment contributes to various degenerative diseases, but whether it occurs in calcified aortic valves and during human valvular interstitial cell (hVIC) osteogenic differentiation remains unknown. We therefore investigated the role of mitophagy in CAVD and whether its pharmacological treatment prevents disease progression. Methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on human aortic valves and hVICs. TJ0113, a novel orally available mitophagy activator from our previous screening, was tested in two CAVD mouse models. Multi-omics analyses and functional rescue experiments were performed to elucidate the mechanism. Results: Mitophagy was impaired in calcified human aortic valves and during hVIC osteogenic differentiation. TJ0113 activated MCL1-mediated mitophagy and attenuated disease progression in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, the mitophagy receptor MCL1 anchors a fraction of PRMT3 on mitochondria. During osteogenic differentiation, a dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication is initiated by the increased release of PRMT3 into the cytosol, where it interacts with BACH1 and impairs BACH1 nuclear translocation. This leads to a widespread loss of BACH1 genomic occupancy, relieving BACH1-mediated transcriptional repression of the pro-osteogenic factor PARM1 and promoting hVIC osteogenic differentiation. Mitophagy activation by TJ0113 restored MCL1-PRMT3 binding and reversed these alterations. Conclusions: Mitophagy impairment drives CAVD through dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication mediated by the MCL1-PRMT3-BACH1-PARM1 axis. Pharmacological mitophagy activation by TJ0113 corrects this communication and attenuates disease progression, representing a promising therapeutic strategy for CAVD.

papers.title: Biomechanical stress in the retinal pigment epithelium surrounding laser scars in humans
papers.abstract: Purpose : The wound response of an epithelium comprises tissue-scale activation of stress fibers whose contraction regionally reconfigures the epithelium and drives closure of the wound. Recent in vitro studies have shown that similar biomechanical processes can paradoxically lead to enlargement of epithelial holes. In patients having undergone laser photocoagulation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), laser scars may expand over years. Here, to document the implication of epithelial biomechanics in the enlargement of laser scars we analyzed the dynamic changes affecting the RPE around scars in patients and performed confocal microscopy on a RPE flat-mount from a donor eye. Methods: We analyzed the image files of five patients (age 61 to 85 years) showing enlargement of laser scars in the RPE (follow-up, 13 to 60 months). In three of them, prospective imaging was performed using transscleral illumination adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO), an imaging technology enabling visualization of RPE cells. Time-lapse sequences were analyzed to track dynamic processes in the RPE surrounding scars. A flat-mounted phalloidin-labeled RPE from a human donor eye with a history of scatter photocoagulation was examined by confocal microscopy to document the distribution of stress fibers and cell metrics. Results: Time-lapse sequences showed that enlargement of laser scars was accompanied by the displacement of microscopic features in margins of atrophy. AOO imaging suggested locally coordinated displacement of mosaic of darks spots, with a generally radial or tangent direction relative to the edges of scars. Such movements were detected up to several hundred microns from the edges of scars. On the histology sample, elongated RPE cells with stress fibers forming actin cables were found along edges of scars, which formed fascicles between adjacent scars. Conclusion: Enlargement of RPE scars may be accompanied by long-lasting, largescale changes in the distribution of microscopic features in the margins of lesions. In particular, transscleral illumination AOO showed coordinated displacement of a mosaic similar to the one described for the RPE. The finding by histology of RPE cell with a tractional phenotype along edges further suggests that epithelial biomechanics contribute to such movements and may hence contribute to scar enlargement.

papers.title: Loss of stromal VEGFR2 protects against ischemic acute kidney injury by preserving the renal microvasculature
papers.abstract: Injury to the renal microvasculature, particularly the peritubular capillaries, is a defining feature of ischemic acute kidney injury (AKI). Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) signaling is a central regulator of endothelial cell survival, proliferation, migration, and vascular remodeling. Although VEGFR2 has been extensively studied in endothelial cells, accumulating evidence suggests that it is also expressed in non-endothelial cell populations, where it may regulate tissue-specific responses to injury. Here, using publicly available single-cell or single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human and mouse kidneys, we identified VEGFR2 expression in renal stromal populations. Immunostaining further detected phosphorylated VEGFR2 in the renal stroma of mouse kidneys. To determine the functional role of stromal VEGFR2, we utilized renal stroma-specific Vegfr2 KO mice. Stromal VegfR2 deletion attenuated kidney injury after renal ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI), as evidenced by reduced tubular injury, preservation of renal blood flow, decreased endothelial oxidative stress, and maintenance of the renal microvasculature. Stromal Vegfr2-deficient kidneys also exhibited increased Angpt1 and Tek levels, enhanced endothelial ERK activation, and preserved endothelial adherent junctions. Taken together, these findings reveal an unexpected role for VEGFR2 in the renal stromal lineage and highlight stromal-endothelial communication as a potential therapeutic target for preserving microvascular integrity after ischemic AKI.

papers.title: Digital pathological classification of peripheral neuroblastic tumors across multi-continent cohorts
papers.abstract: Peripheral neuroblastic tumors (pNTs) are embryonal tumors of neural crest origin with highly variable clinical behaviors, ranging from spontaneous regression to aggressive and fatal disease. The International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (INPC) defines four diagnostic categories and stratifies tumors into Favorable Histology (FH) or Unfavorable Histology (UH) group based on age-linked assessment of tumor differentiation/maturation and the Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index (MKI). Prognostic distinction according to INPC offers significant prediction of clinical outcomes, with patients harboring FH tumors demonstrating longer overall and event-free survival than those with UH tumor. Here, we assembled the largest multi-continental whole-slide histology imaging dataset of pNTs to date, comprising 2,030 tumors from the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany and Japan. Using this dataset, we developed NB-PathAssist, a computational pathology framework for automated INPC-based classification from digitized whole-slide images. NB-PathAssist integrates foundation-model-based feature extraction with an archetype-guided SummaryMixing architecture that compresses whole-slide morphology into representative histologic tokens for tumor-level classification. To automate MKI assessment, we manually annotated 14,049 nuclei, classifying them as mitotic-karyorrhectic (MK) tumor cells, non-MK tumor cells, or non-tumor cells. The resulting model was applied to phenotype cells in whole-slide images across 1,649 tissue sections. Across geographically and institutionally diverse cohorts, NB-PathAssist reproducibly assessed key diagnostic features and generated prognostic classifications concordant with reference INPC annotations. The average balanced accuracy for classifying tumor categories, grade of neuroblastic differentiation, MKI and prognostic groups achieved 0.84, 0.86, 0.89 and 0.96, respectively. We packaged the NB-PathAssist algorithms into an end-to-end online platform for scalable and standardized AI-assisted assessment of pNTs.

papers.title: Epidemic Risks associated with high-temperature replicating infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) field isolates: from molecular characterization to host pathogen interactions
papers.abstract: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) is a WOAH-notifiable pathogen responsible for severe acute disease in salmonids at temperatures ranging from 4 to 14{degrees}. At higher water temperatures, the disease is generally associated with reduced mortality and lower viral replication. In the context of climate change, rising water temperatures could favor the emergence of thermotolerant strains while representing a major physiological and metabolic stress potentially altering fish's immune responses. This study aims to characterize the impact of increasing water temperatures on IHNV replication and host-pathogen interactions. Following pre-screening, the replication kinetics of the reference strain N61 and two field isolates RtNag0a and SA-22 were characterized in EPC (Epithelioma Papulosum Cyprini) and RTG-2 (Rainbow trout gonad) cell lines at 14, 20 and 22{degrees}. Virulence and host-pathogen interactions were subsequently investigated in vivo in zebrafish (Zf) larvae using complementary microinjection and bath immersion infection models at 21.5 and 23.5{degrees}. In vitro studies revealed distinct thermal replication profiles, distinguishing thermosensitive from thermotolerant isolates, although these phenotypes were influenced by the cellular environment. The zebrafish model enabled the characterization of virulence and antiviral host responses associated with thermotolerant IHNV isolates. Notably, waterborne infection proved effective, contrasting with previous reports describing this exposure route as unsuitable for IHNV studies. These findings expand the growing list of emerging European IHNV genotypes capable of replicating at elevated temperatures (>20{degrees}) and establish zebrafish larvae as a relevant model for virulence assessment of field isolates. Together, these results provide valuable insights into the potential impact of climate warming on IHNV epidemiology and support efforts to predict and anticipate future outbreaks under changing environmental conditions.

papers.title: Arthroscopic Raman Probe Provides Biomarkers of TMJ Tissue Composition that Account for Tissue Function
papers.abstract: Background: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders affect up to 25% of the population and may require diverse surgical interventions. However, intraoperative decision-making relies largely on visual assessment, which does not quantitatively characterize tissue composition or mechanical function. Raman spectroscopy offers a nondestructive approach to molecular-level tissue characterization, but its application to TMJ tissues remains unvalidated. Methods: An arthroscopy-compatible Raman probe was used to characterize mandibular condyles (n=15 porcine, n=11 human) and human articular discs (n=7). Raman-derived biomarkers associated with glycosaminoglycans (GAG), collagen (COL), water (H2O), and hydroxyapatite (HA) were evaluated against condylar indentation modulus and disc tensile modulus. Arthroscopic measurements in cadaveric TMJs assessed technical feasibility, while hyperspectral Raman imaging characterized spatial compositional distributions. Results: For condylar cartilage, combined GAG and H2O biomarkers accounted for 86% of the variation in indentation modulus (R2=0.86), compared with 4% for Outerbridge grading (R2=0.04). For articular discs, combined proline and water-associated biomarkers accounted for 88% of the variation in tensile modulus (R2=0.88). Raman spectra acquired in situ under simulated arthroscopic conditions were comparable in quality to ex vivo measurements. Raman imaging revealed distinct compositional patterns in healthy and degenerated tissues, including GAG depletion and cartilage thinning in degenerated condylar cartilage. Conclusions: Raman-derived biomarkers are strongly associated with TMJ cartilage and disc mechanical properties and outperform Outerbridge grading in explaining variation in condylar indentation modulus. Arthroscopic Raman spectroscopy is technically feasible and may complement visual assessment by providing objective compositional information to support future development of tissue-informed surgical decision-making.

papers.title: Spectroscopy-Based Machine Learning to Predict Stem-End Rot in Avocados with the Temporal Effects
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of postharvest fruit quality is essential for reducing food waste and improving supply chain efficiency. This study investigates the integration of spectral information and temporal dynamics for predicting stem-end rot in avocados using hyperspectral Vis-NIR data. Three modelling approaches were compared: a feedforward neural network using only spectral information, an extended model incorporating storage duration, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) encoding a first-order kinetic constraint. To evaluate temporal extrapolation, models were trained on samples from early storage stages and tested on day-12 data. Results show that while spectral data provide strong predictive capability, incorporating time as a simple input can lead to overfitting. In contrast, the PINN improves generalization by guiding learning with mechanistic knowledge, achieving the best performance on unseen temporal conditions. These findings highlight the value of combining data-driven and physics-based approaches, offering a promising pathway toward more robust and interpretable models for time-dependent food quality assessment.

papers.title: Management of Root-Knot Nematode-Fusarium Wilt Complex with different Bio-management methods in Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) var Srijana
papers.abstract: The root-knot nematode-Fusarium complex is a major constraint to protected tomato cultivation in Nepal, particularly on the widely grown Srijana hybrid, which lacks Mi-mediated nematode resistance. The present study was conducted to identify the most effective biocontrol agent, to identify the most effective Solanum rootstock, and to compare the overall efficacy of grafting versus biocontrol agents under polyhouse conditions. For the management of the root knot nematode-Fusarium complex, a pot experiment was set up in a completely randomized design at Pokhara, Kaski. Treatments comprised Trichoderma viride, Pseudomonas fluorescens, their half-dose combination, self-grafted Srijana, and four resistant rootstocks (S. sisymbriifolium, S. melongena, S. torvum, and VNRRs-10), together with nematode-only, Fusarium-only, complex (Nematode + Fusarium), and disease-free controls. Each plant was inoculated with approximately 2,000 nematode eggs, followed by 25 ml of 10^6 spores per ml of Fusarium seven days later to mimic the field complex. Plant growth parameters and nematode infestation data were recorded and analyzed via RStudio v. 2026.04.0. The root knot nematode-Fusarium complex caused significantly greater reductions in vegetative biomass than root knot nematode and Fusarium alone (20.32 gm vs 38.40 gm vs 51.32 gm) at 45 DAT. Single-agent biocontrol gave intermediate protection (T. viride 64.9%; P. fluorescens 47.9% nematode management efficiency), whereas combined T. viride + P. fluorescens treatment produced the highest vegetative biomass but the weakest nematode suppression (320 galls, reproduction factor: 38). Grafting onto S. torvum and S. melongena resulted in the greatest nematode suppression, achieving 97.9% and 93.6% management efficiency, respectively, while S. torvum alongside VNRRs-10 maintained the highest Fusarium suppression (92.5%). Overall resistant rootstocks consistently outperformed biological control in reducing disease severity. These findings indicate that grafting onto resistant solanum rootstocks, particularly S. torvum and S. melongena, was observed as the most effective strategy for managing the root knot nematode-Fusarium complex under protected cultivation, offering a viable chemical-free management option. Keywords: Root-Knot Nematode, Fusarium oxysporum, RKN-Fusarium-complex, Solanum torvum

papers.title: Host response against SARS-CoV-2 infection is impacted by allosteric modulation of cholinergic and purinergic receptors
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused nearly 8 million deaths and a broad spectrum of clinical manifestations driven by dysregulated host inflammation, notably involving key signalling proteins IL-6, CXCL10, and CXCL5. We previously demonstrated that ivermectin (IVM) improves clinical outcomes and reduces the IL-6/IL-10 ratio in the lungs of SARS-CoV-2-infected hamsters. Here, combining high-throughput confocal microscopy and transcriptomics in human cell co-cultures and a hamster model, we dissected how IVM modulates host cells responses via 7nAChR and purinergic receptors. In vitro, IVM acted independently of 7nAChR, instead triggering a P2X4-dependent drop in intracellular ATP, rapidly upregulating CXCL10 in macrophages, and suppressing CXCL5 and IL-6. In vivo, however, 7nAChR antagonists abolished IVMs clinical benefit, as did the P2X4 blocker BX430; moreover, whereas the orthosteric agonist EVP-6124 was ineffective, the positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) IVM and GAT-107 reduced lung pathology and anosmia. Thus, IVM operates through a dynamic, context-dependent interplay: P2X4 drives early innate responses in cellular systems including macrophages, whereas the situation in vivo is more complex with 7nAChR being essential for tissue protection. These data position selective PAMs and the CXCL10/CXCL5 axis as promising targets for host-directed therapy in COVID-19.

papers.title: Targeting the Kidneys Osmotic Gradient with AVPR2 Antagonism Limits Inflammation and Fibrosis after Injury
papers.abstract: Introduction: Arginine vasopressin receptor 2 (AVPR2) signaling regulates kidney collecting duct signaling and urinary concentration, but the kidneys cell-type-specific responses to its pharmacological inhibition and their relevance to non-cystic kidney injury remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We examined physiological and transcriptional responses to the AVPR2 antagonist Tolvaptan in uninjured male mice and assessed tissue outcomes after unilateral ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and repeated cisplatin administration. Analyses included renal tissue osmolality measurements, single nucleus and bulk RNA sequencing of kidney tissues, quantitative PCR, in situ hybridization, and histology. Results: In uninjured kidneys, Tolvaptan reduced urine and medullary tissue osmolality and altered transcription predominantly in medullary collecting-duct populations, including lower expression of selected stress-associated and proinflammatory genes. Following IRI, Tolvaptan-treated mice exhibited attenuated expression of inflammatory and monocyte recruitment genes, reduced macrophage accumulation in the renal medulla, and diminished fibrotic remodeling. In cisplatin-induced kidney injury Tolvaptan reduced tubular injury markers and inflammatory activation in the outer medulla. Conclusions: Tolvaptan attenuates medullary tubular stress responses and post-injury inflammation and fibrosis. These findings extend the effects of pharmacological AVPR2 antagonism beyond water homeostasis to tissue-level responses in non-cystic kidney injury.

papers.title: Histological morphometric correlates of MRI-defined cortical thinning in temporal lobe epilepsy
papers.abstract: Large-scale MRI studies have consistently demonstrated progressive and age-accelerated neocortical thinning in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE). These findings are frequently interpreted as evidence of cumulative neurodegeneration. However, the histopathological substrates underlying MRI-confirmed cortical thinning in epilepsy remain poorly defined. In particular, it is unknown whether cortical thinning reflects irreversible neuronal loss or potentially reversible epilepsy-related network alterations in cortical microstructure. We analysed the resected middle temporal gyrus from 117 individuals undergoing surgery for temporal lobe epilepsy, including cases with (n= 74) or without hippocampal sclerosis (HS) and 12 cases with additional temporal lobe sclerosis (TLS, or Focal Cortical Dysplasia IIIa), defined by a distinct pattern of cytoarchitectural reorganisation and gliosis involving superficial layers. All cases were stratified by the presence or absence of pre-operative MRI-defined cortical thinning of the middle temporal gyrus, quantified using CAT12 relative to healthy controls. On NeuN-immuno-labelled sections using automated image analysis we assessed neuronal spatial distributions relative to their size and packing density; relative cortical layer thickness and sulcal-gyral cytoarchitectural variation were also quantified. MRI-defined cortical thinning was not associated with diffuse neuronal loss. Instead, thinning correlated with increased neuronal density and altered cell-size spatial organisation in superficial and deep layers, particularly in right temporal lobe epilepsy cases with HS. There was limited evidence of layer-specific laminar thinning, being confined to layer VI in the right TLE/HS group only. Of note, TLS cases did not show either cortical thinning on MRI or laminar thinning on histology compared to cases without TLS but altered neuronal densities and composition that was not confined to the superficial cortex. MRI cortical thinning was also characterised by attenuation of normal sulcal/gyral cytoarchitectural variations suggesting disruption of cortical architectural gradients. In contrast, cases with HS but without MRI cortical thinning demonstrated loss of the expected inter-hemispheric cytoarchitectural asymmetry, indicating a distinct pathological process dissociated from thinning. Clinical-pathological correlations were lateralised, including age of onset, further supporting distinct mechanisms contributing to MRI cortical thinning between left and right TLE. These findings challenge the prevailing assumption that MRI-defined cortical thinning in epilepsy reflects progressive neuronal degeneration. Rather than laminar neuronal loss and atrophy, thinning was associated with altered neuronal packing and cell-size distributions between layers. This points towards altered neuropil volumes, including myelin content and dendritic remodelling, in turn suggesting potentially reversible dynamic seizure- or network-related processes.
